about.title: Delivering honest, affordable and quality driven auto and truck repair since 1982
text: Gulf Coast Auto & Truck Repair of League City is your one-stop auto and truck repair shop. Our mission is to provide you with the absolute best service at a competitive price while doing so in a timely manner. From sub-compacts to class 7 commercial trucks, we are equipped and trained to handle all your repair needs.

The mission of the management and master certified technical teams at Gulf Coast Auto and Truck Repair is to correctly repair your vehicle on its first visit, to do so at a price that is affordable, and to perform those repairs in a timely manner. In addition, we promise never to upcharge or sell you repairs that your vehicle does not need.

Our shop is set up to be an integral part of the Clear Lake and Bay Area communities. For more than 35 years we have kept the residents and businesses in this area operating in good condition, and we have been providing quality service and repair for the greater Bay Area for over 40 years.

facts.heading: Questions we are asked often
items: Do I have to go to the dealership for repairs or scheduled maintenance? No. The law requires the factory to honor your warranty as long as you have proper documentation of the appropriate maintenance. Have any legitimate mechanic do the work, keep your records and receipts, and have the mechanic sign your maintenance schedule book if you have one.

Is my vehicle safe to drive? Call the shop before you drive it. We can assess the situation well enough to tell you whether it is safe to drive or needs to be towed, and if there is any question we will help you arrange to get it towed here.
Car care tips for summer and winter weather, long trips, fuel economy, oil change intervals and RV care are on our Car Care Tips page.

facts.heading: Useful vehicle info
facts.text: Check your vehicle for recalls at Safercar.gov, using the VIN. Vehicles are lasting longer: the average vehicle on the road is 11.5 years old, and drivers do not need to think about a new one until it approaches 200,000 miles. AAA studies compute that the depreciation from replacing a vehicle too early costs 2.5 times more than all the insurance payments made during the life of a vehicle, so holding on to your later model vehicle makes excellent financial sense.
